chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You [combine the Maghrib and 'Isha prayers] during the time of Maghrib when traveling a distance of up to five miles after sunset.'

key_terms.خَمْسَةِ أَمْيَالٍ: Five miles (a specific distance for travel rulings)

ai.seo_question: When can a traveler combine Maghrib and Isha prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific temporal boundary for *Jam' al-Ta'khir* (delayed combination) of Maghrib and 'Isha during travel, establishing that the window extends until one has traveled approximately five miles after sunset. This distance serves as a practical metric in Shia fiqh to determine when the traveler has sufficiently moved to justify combining the prayers, reflecting the juristic emphasis on ease (*rukhas*) for the traveling Muslim.
